appraisal_events.evidence: Léonie announces that Eulalie will not come and is flatly corrected by her servant (Mais il n’est pas cinq heures, madame Octave, il n’est que quatre heures et demie); she answers a dim afternoon with cosmic indignation (il faut que le bon Dieu soit bien en colère après nous); and when Eulalie finally arrives, Une vive rougeur animait les joues de ma tante ... Malheureusement, à peine venait-elle d’être introduite que Françoise rentrait with the Curé’s message.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator stages Léonie's whole day as a miniature comedy of misjudgment and thwarted pleasure: she is wrong about the hour, disproportionate about the weather, and the one visit she has been waiting for is spoiled at the very moment it begins. The flattering wrapper of the Curé's message (enchanté, ravi, ne veut pas déranger) only sharpens the irony, since the deference itself is what displaces her pleasure.

appraisal_events.evidence: avec un sourire qui avait pour but de se mettre elle-même à l’unisson de la joie qu’elle ne doutait pas que ses paroles allaient causer à ma tante, articulant les syllabes pour montrer que ... elle rapportait, en bonne domestique, les paroles mêmes dont avait daigné se servir le visiteur.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator undercuts Françoise's self-satisfied performance of the perfect servant: the reader has already been told Malheureusement, so her confident anticipation of her mistress's joy is exposed as a misreading, and her syllable-by-syllable fidelity reads as officious display rather than tact.

status_effects.explanation: Her long-anticipated pleasure in Eulalie's visit is cancelled at the instant it arrives, leaving her worse off emotionally than before the flush of joy.
She is shown comically mistaken about the hour and inflating a grey afternoon into divine vengeance, which lowers how she is locally appraised.
Her complacent good-servant performance is ironized: she smiles in advance at a joy the narration has already marked as spoiled.

ambiguities: The figure who drives the local reversal, M. le Curé, is descriptor-identified rather than named and does not appear on the reference sheet, so he is omitted from characters_present per the scope rules even though his announcement is what spoils Léonie's pleasure; if he were admitted, the passage would also support a positive deference event from him toward Léonie (serait enchanté, ravi ... ne veut pas déranger).

The Octave of mon pauvre Octave is tante Léonie's dead husband, quoted as a pious authority, and is not the reference sheet's Octave (the Balbec dandy); he is treated here as a trivial mention-only reference and omitted rather than registered as an unresolved character.
